learning_outcomes.text: Be able to propose and plan the resolution of engineering problems, following the standard procedures used in technical and scientific environments.
Be able to express oneself with appropriate correctness and precision for the engineering technological environment.
Be able to express the center of mass and the moment of inertia of a body and calculate it for simple geometries.
Be able to analyze, formalize, and solve problems involving vibratory motion or wave motion.
Be able to formalize and solve basic problems in kinematics, statics, and dynamics. Know how to apply Newton's laws and the conservation laws of mechanics.
Be able to calculate, for a simple thermodynamic system, the heat absorbed or released, the work done, as well as its internal energy.
Know and be able to apply the measurement process of physical magnitudes involved in an experiment, and know how to correctly express and represent the results of said process.

syllabus_topics: Vectors in Euclidean affine space (ℝ3, +, .). Basic vector operations. Sliding vectors. Systems of sliding vectors. Bound vectors. Systems of bound vectors. Differentiation and integration with vectors. Gradient, divergence, and curl.

Rectilinear motion. Curvilinear motion. Tangential and normal components of acceleration. Circular motion: angular velocity. Non-Cartesian coordinates: velocity and acceleration in plane polar, spherical, and cylindrical coordinates. Relative motion.

Newton's laws of motion: concepts of mass and force. Contact forces. Normal force. Tension. Force exerted by a spring: Hooke's Law. Friction forces between surfaces. Non-inertial reference frames. Fictitious forces. Energy formulation of mechanics. Work and kinetic energy. Position-dependent forces: potential energy. Conservation of mechanical energy.
Systems of particles. Center of mass: solids, composite bodies. Conservation laws of linear momentum, angular momentum, and energy in systems of particles.
Equilibrium conditions. Bodies in equilibrium. Reactions at supports and contacts. Free body diagram. Cables.

Rotation about a fixed axis: moment of inertia. Analogies with rectilinear motion. Conservation of angular momentum. Calculation of moments of inertia. Steiner's and perpendicular axis theorems. The inertia tensor. Kinetic energy. Principal moments of inertia and principal axes.

Simple harmonic motion. Examples. Kinematics and dynamics. Energy of simple harmonic motion. Small oscillations in other physical systems. Superposition of harmonic motions. Damped oscillations: underdamping, critical damping, and overdamping. Forced oscillations: resonance. Coupled oscillations.
Stress and strain. Hooke's Law. Tensile stress. Compressive stress. Shear. Young's modulus. Shear modulus. Bulk modulus.
Introduction. Thermodynamic systems. Walls. Thermodynamic variables. Equation of state. Thermodynamic processes. Zeroth law of thermodynamics. Temperature. Thermometers. Temperature scales.
The concept of work in thermodynamics. Heat. Specific heat. Latent heats. First law of thermodynamics. Applications to the ideal gas model.
